brief: BofA raised its 2026 S&P 500 EPS estimate to $365 (33% growth) and sees $410 in 2027 (12% growth), yet its year-end index target of 7,400 and 12-month target of 7,800 implied roughly 3% downside and 2% upside at the levels prevailing when the research was published, despite the earnings boom. The gap traces to inflation: BofA's equity valuation is consistent with only 1.7% inflation, while its own economists forecast 3.2% in 2026 and 2.4% in 2027; if actual inflation stays above the valuation-implied level, elevated real rates can offset rising profits even as earnings deliver. Concentration compounds the risk: the five largest companies are a record 27% of next-12-month earnings, and semiconductors alone contribute 9.6 of the 15.4 percentage points of consensus 2027 EPS growth (62% of total index growth), while hyperscaler capex growth is expected to slow from over 90% in 2026 to about 35% in 2027. For the bull case to hold, AI must both deliver the earnings already embedded in estimates and generate enough productivity to ease inflation. The Market Ear's own trade: own the sectors getting earnings revisions (energy, cybersecurity) against a short S&P 500 position, rather than an outright index call.
